# Dynamic Instrumentation with rz-frida

This book is a guide to the **rz-frida** plugin for [Rizin](https://rizin.re):
dynamic instrumentation of Android apps and native processes from inside
rizin. Command output in these chapters was captured on live targets.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    subgraph Host
        RZ[rizin]
        PLG[rz-frida plugin]
        FC[frida-core]
    end
    subgraph Target
        AG[injected agent]
        PROC[process under test]
    end
    RZ --> PLG --> FC
    FC <--> AG
    AG --> PROC
```

# How to use this book

- Start with the **Introduction** if you are new to Frida or to rz-frida.
- **First Steps** sets up the lab and opens the first session.
- The **Android Journey** covers the demo app minapp.
- The **Native Journey** covers the same ideas on a host-side C program.
- **Scripting**, **Remote Access**, and **Under the Hood** cover the agent,
  network and gadget targets, and the protocol.
- **Reference** is the command card. **Challenges** are short exercises.

## Conventions

```bash
$ rizin malloc://512
[0x00000000]> Frsj
{"ok":true,"result":{"active":false,"state":"closed"}}
```

Lines starting with `$` run in a shell. Lines starting with
`[0x00000000]>` are typed inside rizin. Everything after them is captured
output. Addresses, process ids and counts change between runs: treat them as
examples and read the values from your own terminal.

Most plugin cmds are JSON-only, so the book uses the `j` forms
(`Froj`, `Frsj`). Only `Frs` and `Fru` also print plain text.

> **Note:** this book documents the rizin plugin only. The Cutter integration
> is a separate frontend over the same backend and is not covered here.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Try

Most chapters end with a short task you can run along with the text.
:::
